content_metadata.description: A video featuring a Buddhist monk discussing the concept of interconnectedness in Buddhism.

qAndA.question: What is the color of the over-robe worn by the Monk?

qAndA.answer: He brings his hands together and interlaces his fingers, symbolizing how everything is intertwined.
qAndA.question: What gesture does the Monk use to illustrate interconnectedness?

qAndA.answer: He defines emptiness as the lack of an independent self-nature, highlighting that individuals are not isolated entities but exist in relation to everything else.
qAndA.question: How does the Monk define "emptiness" in this context?

qAndA.answer: The Monk advocates for understanding and embodying the Buddhist concept of interconnectedness, emphasizing that everything in the universe, including ourselves, exists in a state of mutual dependence.
qAndA.question: What is the overall message the Monk is conveying?

qAndA.answer: His peaceful presence enhances the message of interconnectedness, conveying a sense of harmony and tranquility that arises from recognizing our interconnected nature.
qAndA.question: What is the significance of the Monk's calm demeanor and tone of voice?

youtube_description:
Shohaku Okumura is a Zen Buddhist Abbot in the Soto Zen tradition.  He lives in Bloomington, Indiana and teaches in the Sanshin Zen Community:  https://www.sanshinji.org/

Subscribe to Interior Mythos Journeys @https://www.youtube.com/c/Interiormythos 

Our Mission: The curriculum of Interior Mythos Journeys is a quest to explore contemporary mythic language that is in harmony with the 21st Century, Global, Quantum Scientific, and Universal Reality in which we all actually live.  Learn more at https://www.https://interiormythos.com/

As we solitarily and collectively claim the force of a relevant contemporary mythos, we are delivered to the possibility of life-lived-in-depth, the possibility of authentic life. This is the path beneath the surface.

The Transformative Encounter: The Practice of Contemplation

In the current age this transformative encounter, as well as the practices that deliver us to this encounter and the personal connection that flows from this encounter, is seldom the focus of our lives. Many of us wander disoriented through life, often on a self-destructive path, in a world seen, understood, and measured primarily by the external environment. We are disconnected from the Connecting Myth. We are disconnected from the interior depth to which the Connecting Myth might deliver us. Ironically, we have come to understand myth as a lie rather than a symbolic and metaphoric gateway to a deeper truth.
